target.name: Roam Robotics
target.founder: Tim Swift, Mallory Ulaszek, Saul Griffith

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $16M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Roam Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $16.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private robotics firms and one public equity comparable, spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling, using the $16M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $33M. The peer-median method references four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed)—yielding a median implied valuation of $1.7B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The substantial divergence between stage-progression ($33M) and peer-median ($1.7B) results reflects the significant heterogeneity within the robotics sector at comparable stages. A triangulated range of $28M to $2.0B (with median at $866M) captures this uncertainty. The median estimate should be viewed as an upper-bound anchor given that Roam's Series A stage positions it below most peer comparables. Key sensitivities include the maturity and revenue profile of peer companies relative to Roam, and whether peer valuations reflect fundamental unit economics or sector exuberance.
